## USB Drive Inventory Collector 4.3.0

This release carries forward the 4.0.0–4.2.9 release history and adds fixes made since the consolidated 4.2.9 notes.

### Windows Application

- Added a native Windows GUI distributed as a self-contained, signed x64 executable. It opens directly, requests administrator access, and offers to install smartmontools with WinGet when it is missing.
- Combined the GUI and terminal workflows in one executable. Terminal runs in its own tab or in a separate console with `--terminal`; the standalone PowerShell collector was removed.
- Added pause and resume controls, activity and version details, per-session logging, notification sounds with a saved mute setting, and an AutoPlay prompt that restores the prior setting on normal exit.
- Made the embedded Terminal accept commands and prompt answers, share the scan pause state with the GUI, and keep its enable/disable control visible while it is running. Added paused-state feedback and refined the Terminal and Workbook Setup layouts.
- Added a Finish screen with the saved workbook location and controls to copy the path, open its folder, or close the app.

### Drive Detection and Entry

- Detects USB-connected physical drives while excluding Windows boot and system disks. Automatic identification uses smartmontools autodetection and transport fallbacks for common USB storage bridges.
- Improved NVMe, SATA, IDE, and PATA identification; added SAT 12-byte pass-through for compatible adapters. Probe results are logged by transport to help diagnose incomplete reads and timeouts.
- Increased the smartmontools process timeout to 30 seconds, corrected the JSON command option, and improved fallback handling after a cached transport times out.
- Skips empty USB docks and card readers until Windows reports media with a usable size. Handles the array of operational statuses returned by Windows Storage WMI.
- Expanded manual drive entry with a searchable, alphabetized list covering SAS, IDE, PATA, floppy, SD, CompactFlash, eMMC, and other media types. Choose **Other** to enter a custom type.
- Added input validation, uppercase model and serial values, `N/A` for blank fields, review and edit steps, duplicate-serial checks and correction, and Copy Last Drive for records with different serial numbers.

### Workbook and Recorded Drives

- Saves records to XLSX after each drive without Excel automation. Workbook Setup lets users choose optional identity columns and separate workbook and log locations.
- Writes each workbook save to a temporary file, validates it before replacing the previous copy, and retries if a save fails.
- Adds a build check that generates a sample workbook, reads it back, validates its Open XML structure, and checks it with an independent spreadsheet reader.
- Added Recorded Drives, Activity, and Terminal views. Recorded Drives supports sorting, display-only row numbers, and double-click editing of the right record, including after sorting.
- When records are sorted by the display-only row number, newly saved records appear at the top. The row number remains outside the workbook data.
- Added Reset View, workbook refresh, path copy, and folder controls. Refined grid sizing, scrolling, editing, and footer layout.
- Added workbook error reporting that distinguishes a successful drive read from a failed workbook update.

### Interface Polish

- Restored distinct tones for saved drives, duplicates, and errors. Notifications are paced, pending tones stop when scanning is paused or sounds are muted, and Terminal enable and disable have separate confirmation tones.
- Fades the status panel through soft blue while reading, soft yellow for duplicate warnings, and soft red for errors.
- Restored the embossed Version Information details box, kept its links clickable, included the full executable filename for copying, and removed build hash text from the displayed version heading.
- Corrected the **Save & Copy** button label and adjusted the sound icon and workbook refresh button alignment.

### Distribution

- Publishes a versioned Windows release, signs the executable, verifies the publisher, and includes a SHA-256 checksum. Pull requests produce unsigned preview builds for testing.
